observe/attempt_1/response.json.content:
Answer: B) The bilateral alveolar infiltrates are predominantly in the lower lobes and the middle lobe of the right lung, consistent with pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, despite the absence of restrictive impairment in pulmonary function tests.

Reason: Both Figure 1a (PA view) and Figure 1b (lateral view) show bilateral, patchy alveolar opacities with relative sparing of the upper lobes; the right middle lobe is involved (visible as a triangular opacity anteriorly on PA and overlapping the heart on lateral), and lower lobes are prominently affected—this distribution matches option B’s description and is characteristic of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, whereas other options misstate lobe involvement (e.g., A, F claim unilateral; C claims upper lobes; E claims diffuse homogeneous involvement).
